questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Oslo as my study destination because they offered a number of cources that i cannot get at my home faculty and I had heard many good things from previous exchange students about the program here.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Both KU and UiO have been great at informing about all the necessary things

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A week before the semester started we had i Buddy-week for all the incoming international students. Here we both got information about the most bacis things we needed to know, got to see the faculty and city, and got a chance to connect with other exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was fine. I looked at both
Finn.no
and
Hybel.no
and found something quit fast.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is much cheaper to live on campus, so that should definitely be taken into consideration when choosing to find something off campus. However, it is easier to find something off campus in the city than getting a student accommondation in the city (most exchange-students lives in Sogn or Kringsjå).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registred my wishes for courses in Studentweb when the course-registration opened in June.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UiO sent me mails with clear instruction on what to do when

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register your wishes for course as soon as possible when the registration opens. Then you have a better chance of getting the courses that you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found that my host university had a good selection of courses. However, I only had two-three lectures a week with i found a little less than i prefer, as there is a lot of self study instead.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two MA classes and one BA class (which however followed the MA course but just had a shorter exam and syllabus)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at UiO is mostly lectures - no seminars. I like that teaching style, nevertheless it would have been nice with some more lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Law and Peace
Maritime Law
EU Competition

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was especially happy with EU Competition law. The professors and their teaching style was really good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't know if it was unexpected but I would say that it is quit expensive to travel around in Norway with train, flight, ect.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices here are quit similar to the danish

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend many organized things myself, but there is really something for everyone

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Both sports, knitting- and readingclubs, dinners for international students, hikes for international students, organized ocean swims, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would say the hikes and dinners are good ways to create a network and get to know the area.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Use it as a change to see the country. I would personally recommend taking the train to Bergen for a weekend, going to Lofoten if you have some extra days off, or to rent a cabin somewhere (both nice in the summer and when the snow starts to fall)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quit easy i would say. Norway is in many ways similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students can be more difficult to get to know - get involved in student activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That was not really an issue to me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love how Norwegians use the nature a lot!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.Remember to travel the country while you are here - there are so many beautiful places 
2.Be open and involve yourself with the other international students - it is so important to socialize when you are away from your normal life 
3. Use the city, there are many great spot for studying, green areas to chill, nice cafes, restaurants etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything specific. Both KU and UiO will guide you through the most.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many new people from all over the would. It has been very inspirerering.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having a lot more freetime than I am used to. You need to fill your weeks with a lot of good plans!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
